batch_strategy: Matched local condition-response and loading contrasts focused on confirmed V2 failure regions, with selected structural controls for transfer across oxygenated, nitrile, sulfoxide, and amine-containing families.

choices.reason: This m116 1/1 row provides the strong-eluent endpoint for a matched solvent-response sequence. Its predicted V1/V2 is 4.39/9.92 mL, complementing measured m116 rows at 2/1 and 20/1 (17418a1ba5c9443057c3, c3eb276f59965c3608f1) and testing whether the local curve is monotone.

This intermediate 5/1 m116 point is predicted at 7.78/14.08 mL. Together with the measured 2/1 and 20/1 endpoints, it can determine whether the observed increase with solvent ratio is gradual or concentrated near one condition boundary.

The 10/1 m116 point, predicted at 10.90/19.14 mL, completes a dense response curve around the confirmed model-direction failure. It supplies high-value supervision for solvent-response interpolation in related dimethoxy aromatics.

This 20/1 m116 row at 150 uL is predicted at 15.81/30.28 mL and adds a higher-load replicate near the measured 20/1 result c3eb276f59965c3608f1. It tests whether the large completion shift is condition-driven or load-dependent.

This m39 0/1 control is predicted at 4.59/9.66 mL, while measured m39 at 5/1 and 150 uL is 10.76/26.72 mL (ae8805bc02bce03072e2). It anchors the weak-eluent side of the m39 response and helps separate solvent effects from loading effects.

This m39 5/1 row at 100 uL is predicted at 13.27/30.02 mL. It is a loading contrast to the measured 5/1, 150 uL row ae8805bc02bce03072e2 and tests whether the broad V2 response transfers to a lower load.

This m39 20/1 row at 150 uL is predicted at 17.50/42.78 mL, extending the solvent curve into a strong-eluent region. It can reveal whether the model underestimates the persistence of late completion for this oxygenated aromatic compound.

The m39 10/1 row provides an intermediate condition point with a predicted broad interval near 14.92/35.85 mL. It links the measured 5/1 result to stronger-eluent behavior and improves learning of endpoint-specific retention changes.

This m107 1/1 row is predicted at 11.58/24.07 mL, contrasting with the measured 5/1 m107 row c6924324ddd95f249df6 at 43.20/101.44 mL. It tests whether the extreme late completion is already present at a weaker eluent or is sharply condition-dependent.

This m107 2/1, 50 uL row is predicted at 27.29/60.24 mL and probes the same multifunctional ether-containing molecule near the measured 5/1 failure. It helps repair the large V1 and V2 underprediction around this chemical family.

This matched m107 2/1 row at 150 uL has nearly the same prediction, 27.28/60.26 mL, as the 50 uL row. Measuring both loads tests whether the unusually broad m107 interval is insensitive to loading or whether the model has missed a loading interaction.

This m107 5/1, 150 uL row is predicted at 45.31/102.25 mL, closely near the measured 5/1, 100 uL result c6924324ddd95f249df6. The paired labels directly quantify loading sensitivity in one of the strongest observed V2 failure regions.

This m199 0/1 row is predicted at 6.39/13.23 mL, contrasting with the measured 2/1 row b060fa3ae84f80e773d2 at 12.32/22.67 mL and the measured 5/1 row 714004602e6452764d9a at 28.52/52.30 mL. It anchors the weak-eluent side of the sulfoxide response.

This m199 1/1 row is predicted at 6.03/13.09 mL and supplies an intermediate solvent point between the measured 0/1 and 2/1 contexts. It tests whether the observed late retention emerges gradually or through a sharp condition-dependent transition.

This m199 5/1, 50 uL row is predicted at 31.30/56.76 mL and forms a loading contrast to measured m199 at 5/1, 100 uL (714004602e6452764d9a). It directly tests whether sulfoxide-associated completion broadening depends on sample amount.

This m199 0/1, 150 uL row is predicted at 2.30/5.07 mL and is a strong loading control against the 0/1, 50 uL candidate b2bf97a1dcb9d6609f7d. Together they can identify whether the large measured m199 shift is molecular-condition behavior or an unmodeled loading effect.

hypotheses.content: Loading amount can change onset and especially completion in a compound-dependent way, with oxygenated aromatic compounds and sulfoxides showing larger interval changes than the predictor currently represents.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Loading amount varies widely across the catalog and may interact with functional-group-specific silica binding. Matched load controls can improve both endpoint prediction and interval-width calibration.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m39 and m199 matched loading contrasts show a reproducible load effect after solvent and molecule are held fixed?

hypotheses.content: Very broad or unexpectedly late completion is compound-specific near strong-eluent conditions; the broad behavior of cinnamic acid does not transfer universally to other oxygenated compounds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: V2 errors dominate several of the largest observed residuals. Condition-response labels from related but chemically distinct oxygenated compounds can prevent an overly universal broadening rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does a strong-eluent response curve for another broad-completion family show persistent V2 elevation or rapid contraction?

hypotheses.content: The predicted decrease in m116 retention from 2/1 to 20/1 was a model-response artifact; measured m116 retention instead increased across that range, and intermediate points are needed to learn the local curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This is a direct matched-molecule solvent-response failure with opposite observed and predicted direction. Intermediate points can correct solvent-response shape for m116 and nearby aromatic ethers.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the observed m116 increase from 2/1 to 20/1 gradual through 1/1, 5/1, and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Functional-group identity and local structural environment cause large retention and interval errors for multifunctional polar compounds and sulfoxides that are not captured by group counts alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These failures affect both V1 and V2 and recur across catalog families. Additional labels can improve structural offsets and interactions among polarity, basicity, loading, and solvent strength.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do additional m107 and m199 labels confirm persistent late completion across their local condition-response curves?

feedback_interpretation: Recent measurements show that V2 is the dominant failure mode in several regions. m107 at 5/1 was measured at 43.20/101.44 mL, m199 reached 28.52/52.30 mL at 5/1, and cinnamic acid reached 108.89 mL completion at 1/1. These results support targeted repair of broad-interval and multifunctional polar rows. The m166 loading comparison also supports compound-dependent loading behavior, although other examples remain mixed. The m116 measurements directly rejected the predicted solvent direction: measured retention increased from 2/1 to 20/1 despite predictions indicating the opposite trend. The corrected batch therefore concentrates on intermediate m116 points and matched loading or solvent contrasts around m39, m107, and m199.
batch_rationale: The batch combines three forms of information that are currently most useful: dense local condition curves for the confirmed m116 response failure, matched loading contrasts for m39, m107, and m199, and solvent anchors around molecules with large observed V2 errors. The m107 and m199 subsets distinguish solvent-response shape from loading sensitivity, while m39 tests whether the oxygenated aromatic loading pattern transfers. The batch also spans weak, intermediate, and strong eluent conditions and supplies labels in regions with broad predicted intervals. These measurements should improve endpoint calibration, interval-width learning, and molecular-condition interactions across recurring Row-distribution families.
